originality.rationale: The equal-side-count CDF is an elementary extension of a previously recorded distinct-side-count tangency-gap law (ed975dc4-7a69-4cf2-8014-37e5f8e7492c) and is NOT separately claimed novel. Neither that prior statement nor the published published-finding corpus expected-area theorem establishes a strict coupled stochastic order across all side counts or its sharp beta-limit correction. Buck–Siddon provide fixed-side-length tangent geometry, O’Rourke–Zaimi side counts. The full 2014 general-rotation paper remained inaccessible, creating an explicit residual priority risk.
residual_risks: The supporting equal-order CDF is subsumed by the direct extension of an earlier unequal-order normal-gap formula; the novel claim must be read specifically as cross-n stochastic order and beta correction.
The 2014 Brazitikos–Stavrakakis article was inaccessible in full despite public author-copy and institutional attempts; its precise special planar subcases cannot be excluded from abstract alone.
Search indexing cannot eliminate earlier unindexed formulas for random rotational overlap.
The elementary tangent-length identity and fixed-n expected area are established background, not claimed original.

value.rationale: Normalized overlap loss is a natural rotational alignment observable for regular convex polygons approximating a circle. The novel content is a strict stochastic comparison simultaneously for all polygon orders, not a trivial recomputation of an already known tangent-gap CDF. A self-contained convexity argument yields this hierarchy, and a sharp beta limit with O(n^-2) correction describes its quantitative geometric calibration; the previously known exact distribution alone does not supply the hierarchy.
